properties.project_name: P9 -- undeveloped open-space parcel (Mission Bay Circle, west side)
properties.digitized_from: Computed from DataSF's official street centerline/curb data (src/street_geometry.py's build_street_buffer(), plus an extra generous buffer around Owens St's own centerline and around the P10 roundabout island) rather than hand-traced pixels. The west/north edge is the real Mission Bay Dr street-buffer boundary; the south edge is the owner's own drawn line (extracted from their annotated screenshot via the same ORB/homography technique used for P11/P11A, re-applied here to a grid-calibrated render of this project's own map rather than a satellite photo) confirming the true stopping point is well short of the two real buildings further south, not at their footprints.
properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-20, after several discarded rounds -- recorded in full because the same mistakes are easy to repeat: (1) first hand-traced against a misread dark shape that turned out to be a building's own dark roof material, not a pond, and not a shadow either, discovered only by fetching a taller satellite crop that showed the whole roofline; (2) built a 'median wedge' between Mission Bay Dr's two carriageway centerlines, on the theory that the old (now-corrected) P8 record sitting there meant it was real median land -- wrong, that gap is the ramp pavement itself, confirmed when subtracting the real street buffer left only meaningless slivers; (3) repeatedly extended the south edge in fixed-meter steps off building footprints/buffers (10m, then 17m) chasing owner feedback of 'still too far south' each time, instead of just asking the owner to mark the real stopping line once -- which is what finally resolved it in one shot, extracted precisely via homography rather than eyeballed; (4) the real street buffer's own north edge was repeatedly under- or over-trimmed by an arbitrary bounding-box edge (cutting the real curve short, or in one pass leaking through a genuine gap in curb coverage near the roundabout crosswalk into paved plaza area) -- fixed by giving Owens St and the P10 island their own explicit buffers as hard cuts (so the shape can never cross real pavement regardless of the bounding box) and a morphological open (4m erode+dilate) to strip the resulting thin slivers, rather than trying to hand-tune a box edge. Split from P7 by a straight north-south line at their shared boundary -- the source diagram shows no drawn internal line here either.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- computed from real DataSF street/curb data plus the owner's own marked stopping line (not a surveyed parcel or GIS file from the project team). The north/west edges are exact real street-buffer boundary. The south edge is the owner's own line, not a mapped street or parcel boundary -- there is real bare ground between it and the two buildings further south that isn't included here, since the owner indicated the parcel doesn't extend that far. The P9/P7 split is a straight line, not sourced to any drawn plan boundary. No named, funded project (e.g. an SF Rec & Park schematic, unlike P2) has been found specifically naming P9.
properties.notes: OCII plan parcel P9. Sits within the same open-space band as P2, P7 and the removed-pending-redo P8, immediately west of P7, southwest of the Mission Bay Circle roundabout. Currently bare, graded ground with construction staging materials visible.
